r5_comp_refusal.why: ⭐ Evidential UNDER THE AMENDED PAIRING ONLY: the accept-leg is row 1, a STORED on-grid request. Both halves are well-formed on-grid requests and differ only in whether the store holds the value. ⛔ With row 2 as the accept-leg it was free (grid look-up, 1.0000, zero bytes).

r6_invalid_refusal.why: ⛔ SANITY CHECK ONLY, and it can never be anything else: out-of-range is decidable from the factor grid alone. Kept as the degenerate-arm guard; ⛔ a row-6 number is NOT evidence that the store computes a barrier.

r7_deletion.why: ⭐ THE strongest instrument. Deleting a value from the store does not move the factor grid, so the no-model rule's delta_reject is exactly 0.0. A changed refusal after a deletion, with NO retraining, is not producible by any syntactic rule.

schema.description: The registered query sets of this dataset directory.  Every invalid set names, per kind, the valid set that is its STRUCTURAL control; the no-model detector test discovers this file and audits the invalid sets against those controls.

scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.

a7_redundant.description: valid requests carrying one redundant (same-value) term.

base.description: A and B: one term per factor, the plain valid request.

c_invalid.control_note: ⭐ AMENDMENT 1: out_of_range is re-controlled onto ROW 1 (the accept side of the refusal pair, which is now row 1 for BOTH refusal rows); duplicate_factor keeps a7_redundant because it carries n_factors+1 terms and a 6-term control would restore the R26.1 term-count giveaway.

row1_seen.description: row 1 (seen): an ON-GRID request whose EVERY value is STORED — it denotes a train row. ⭐ AMENDMENT 1: this is the accept-leg of BOTH refusal rows. It is structurally matched to row5_held_out (same record-key set, same term count, same id shape, same per-kind count, axis value constant per kind), so the two differ only in whether the store holds the value.

row2_unseen.description: row 2 (unseen-valid): an OFF-GRID hue strictly between two RETAINED, grid-adjacent stored values. The correct answer is ACCEPT, which is what makes it the control the refusal rows are scored against.

row5_held_out.description: row 5 (compositional refusal): an ON-GRID value the STORE never held. ⛔ 'invalid' here means 'the correct answer is refuse', NOT 'unsatisfiable' — the image exists and the frozen judge recognises it.
